## Design

### 2026-10-24 – I was working on the schematic for my midi device using an ESP32-S3, and I've realized just how useful making nets and labels really is. For some reason I was thinking that setting them up would take

**1.43h**

I was working on the schematic for my midi device using an ESP32-S3, and I've realized just how useful making nets and labels really is. For some reason I was thinking that setting them up would take a long time but it was actually really quick

Using the basic connector  was also a really interesting method to incorporate 7 capacitive touch pins, and something I wouldn't have really considered without outside help.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/435a8295-ed1a-43d6-ad9d-a399d825bbe1/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-24 – I was working on putting together the basic pcb layout, and the guide gave a whole lot of really interesting tips that I wouldn't have known otherwise. I think I made the traces as clean as possible g

**2.42h**

I was working on putting together the basic pcb layout, and the guide gave a whole lot of really interesting tips that I wouldn't have known otherwise. I think I made the traces as clean as possible given this is my second time doing this.

Apparently keeping the back clear will significantly reduce costs if I want to get it assembled, I don't think I do but I kept the back clear of any complex parts, other than the LEDs which can be hand-soldered

![pcb back Screenshot 2026-10-24 101311](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Xt10ZK7FTi1vKiU37U67a1QQj2rKZWIn/e4d5423bae3a012adc0f252c83d1d217dd0bf2e1d738d61fb6c83b11b5a8b816.png)

![pcb Screenshot 2026-10-24 101253](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Xt10ZK7FTi1vKiU37U67a1QQj2rKZWIn/d48d6466825d22f76faed780637eca4325fdfabf1f5223051c0464aa0ee94c12.png)

I also was informed of the JLCPCB plugin that makes it really easy to get a quote going and makes this process really accessible.

I'm not sure if I want to change the ESP board into a socket, because I do have an esp32 s3 from another project, and that could reduce costs

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/da01f299-fd44-4ee0-b3cf-5c54c426fd72/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-25 – I started creating a matching case for the bottom portion of the device so it would be a bit more resistant to the outside elements, and then I could also have the option to add rubber pads to the bot

**1.78h**

I started creating a matching case for the bottom portion of the device so it would be a bit more resistant to the outside elements, and then I could also have the option to add rubber pads to the bottom of the plastic so it would stick in place better

I'm not sure if I should try and make a sliding top for the enclosure, then it would be a bit easier to keep in storage
